Feature / relationship: CGPA, AptitudeTestScore, SoftSkillsRating, SSC_Marks, HSC_Marks vs placement
Observed pattern: Placed students score higher on all five; Cohen's d from 0.94 (CGPA) to 1.23 (AptitudeTestScore)
Candidate statistical test: Mann-Whitney U (primary) + Welch t-test (sensitivity); effect size: Cohen's d and rank-biserial / AUC
Reason: Scores are bounded, mildly skewed and recorded in coarse steps with many ties, so a rank-based test avoids normality assumptions; Welch handles unequal variances. With n~10k, p-values will be tiny, so effect size is what matters.

Candidate statistical test: Chi-square test of independence (2x2); effect size: odds ratio with CI and phi
Reason: Two binary variables; expected cell counts are large, so the chi-square approximation is valid. Odds ratio gives an interpretable effect size.
